sources.title: SEC Form 13F frequently asked questions
sources.limitation: Current compliance guidance is an audit reference, not a beginning-2026 investor view; historical applicability should be frozen to the benchmark date.
sources.provenance_limitation: Provenance is authority for the reported statement/fact, not truth certainty, private motive or audited investment performance.
sources.coverage_count_unit: one listed source record, not one entire lifetime source family

reporting_boundaries: 13F is generally a quarter-end report filed within 45 days, subject to calendar rules. As of 2026-10-13, the normal Q 3 report is not yet due; Q 2 is the latest ordinary completed reporting cycle, not a live portfolio.
Reportable US-listed positions and eligible ADRs can appear; foreign-listed shares, cash, private businesses and many other instruments are outside this view.
Short stock is omitted and must not be netted against the long holding. Written options are excluded; eligible held puts/calls may appear and must be read by instrument column.
Small exempt positions, confidential treatment and later amendments can make the public table incomplete. Use the restated report where supplied.
Reported investment discretion is at manager/entity level. A share-count change does not identify its human decision maker, transaction day, price, hedge, cash flow or motive.
A 13F market-value denominator is not total investor wealth or fund assets. It cannot establish realized P&L, IRR, cost basis or complete portfolio weights.
research_controls: Freeze publication availability, not the date printed in the speech title. A 2024 speech first verified as uploaded in 2026 is not automatically available at the 2026-start cutoff.
Only information demonstrably public by 2025-12-31 may enter the beginning-2026 evidence set. Later holdings, restatements and interviews belong in an explicitly separate audit/outcome layer.
Evaluate a statement at its original business, instrument, investor role, era and capital constraints. A copied current manager portfolio is not that person’s historical recommendation.
For each investment, separate business result, mark-to-market appreciation, realized return, decision quality and investor attribution. Missing links remain missing.
Alternative explanations such as client flows, mandate limits, delegation, hedges, taxes or option assignment are hypotheses unless independently evidenced.

provenance_legend.P1: Original investor writing/verified account or original regulator/fund/company disclosure, only for facts actually established.
provenance_legend.P2: Authorized original-publisher transcript, verified original archive or producer-account republication; recollections remain retrospective and access completeness is separate.
provenance_legend.S1: Reputable contemporaneous independent report; none used as accepted evidence here.
provenance_legend.S2: Later secondary compilation, attendee notes, biography, translation or analytical reconstruction; discovery only here.
provenance_legend.U: Unverified attribution or unavailable original; not promoted into accepted investor intent.

case_timing_legend.T0: Demonstrably public before the actual decision; public business context is separately distinguished from investor intent.
case_timing_legend.T1: Contemporaneous statement/report within specified decision or holding-observation interval; not proved pre-trade.
case_timing_legend.T2: Later retrospective explanation of an earlier decision.
case_timing_legend.TU: Publication/event relationship to the actual decision unknown, or initial evidence missing. General method claims without a particular security decision remain TU for that relation.

timing_count_policy: T-labels are independent of provenance and historical-publication eligibility. A node may have more than one label if it combines a current observation with a retrospective explanation; counts are nonexclusive and denominators are explicit. No timing label establishes investment intent by itself.
